post.description:
Step 1 — submit email. Creates a preliminary account and sends an
EMAIL_VERIFICATION OTP.

Step 3 — first/last name, phone (required) and optional address.
Authorized by the registration token from email verification.
Step 4 & 5 — set password, activate account, sign in.

Email + password. Customers receive tokens immediately. Admins receive an
OTP challenge (mandatory MFA, SEC-02) and must call /auth/admin/verify-otp.
Admin step 2 — verify the ADMIN_LOGIN OTP using the challenge token.

Verify a Google ID token. Returns tokens if the account is complete, else
a registration token to collect the phone number.

Collect required phone number (and optional address) for a new Google
account, then activate and sign in.
Exchange a valid refresh token for a new token pair (refresh is rotated).
Revoke the presented refresh token.
Step 1 — request a FORGOT_PASSWORD OTP.
Step 3 — set a new password using the reset token from /otp/verify.

Centralized OTP send/resend. The event determines the purpose.
ADMIN_LOGIN is issued only during admin sign-in and is rejected here.

Centralized OTP verify. Branches by event:
  * EMAIL_VERIFICATION -> registration token (continue signup)
  * FORGOT_PASSWORD     -> reset token (set a new password)
ADMIN_LOGIN must be verified via /auth/admin/verify-otp (challenge-bound)
and EMAIL_CHANGE via /users/me/email/confirm (needs the caller's identity).

Change the password of the signed-in account.

Requires the current password. All refresh tokens are revoked (SEC-04), so
the client must sign in again to obtain a fresh session.

Step 1 — send an EMAIL_CHANGE code to the new address.

The account is not modified until the code is confirmed.

Step 2 — confirm the code and move the account to the new email.

All refresh tokens are revoked (SEC-04) since the recovery address changed.
